intro: English puts a direct object after 'meet', 'ride', 'enter', 'call', 'ask' and 'resemble'. Japanese treats these as moving toward a person or place, or facing it, so the noun takes に. を is kept for a thing that is acted on, and for a place that you leave or pass through. Picture an arrow: に is where the arrow points, and を is what it acts on or travels along.

skills.rule: Meet, board, enter, phone, ask, answer, resemble, beat and get used to take に; act on a thing, leave a place, or go through it, and you use を.
skills.explain:
Q1. Is the noun handled, changed, made, used up or looked at? Then を: 本を読む, 窓を開ける.

Q2. Is it a person or place you go to, meet, face or end up in or on? Then に. The verbs to learn are 会う, 乗る, 入る, 着く, 電話する, 聞く (ask a person), 答える, 似ている, 勝つ, 負ける, 慣れる, 気づく, 参加する, 反対する and 賛成する: 友達に会う, 電車に乗る, 質問に答える.

Q3. Is it a place you leave or move along? Then を: 部屋を出る, 電車を降りる, 公園を散歩する, 道を渡る. The pairs are worth memorising: 部屋に入る / 部屋を出る, 電車に乗る / 電車を降りる.

A verb can take both, one for each role: 先生に質問をする ('ask the teacher a question'), 母に手紙を書く. The person takes に and the thing takes を. 会う also takes と when two people arranged to meet.
patterns: [person] に [会う / 電話する / 聞く / 勝つ]
[vehicle / room] を [降りる / 出る]

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]{に}会[あ]いました。
examples.en: I met a friend at the station.

examples.jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]バス{に}乗[の]ります。
examples.en: I take the bus every morning.

examples.jp: 次[つぎ]の駅[えき]で電車[でんしゃ]{を}降[お]ります。
examples.en: I get off the train at the next station.

examples.jp: 毎晩[まいばん]母[はは]{に}電話[でんわ]します。
examples.en: I call my mother every evening.

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]{に}質問[しつもん]{を}しました。
examples.en: I asked the teacher a question.

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]は父[ちち]{に}よく似[に]ています。
examples.en: My younger brother looks a lot like our father.

contrast.note: を marks what the verb acts on, or the route or exit point of a movement. 友達を会う and バスを乗る are wrong, because a friend and a bus are not acted on.
に marks the person or place the action goes to. With leaving verbs it fails: 部屋に出る is wrong, because 出る takes を for the room you leave.
With 会う, と is a meeting you arranged together: 友達と会う. に is 'go and see someone' or 'run into someone'. Both are correct, and the English meaning is the same.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]、友達[ともだち]{を}会[あ]いました。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]、友達[ともだち]{に}会[あ]いました。
mistakes.note: 会う takes the person met with に (or と), never を.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]までタクシー{を}乗[の]りました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]までタクシー{に}乗[の]りました。
mistakes.note: You get onto a vehicle: に. Only getting off (降りる) takes を.

mistakes.bad: 八時[はちじ]に部屋[へや]{に}出[で]ました。
mistakes.good: 八時[はちじ]に部屋[へや]{を}出[で]ました。
mistakes.note: 出る takes を for the place you leave.

skills.tip: Going in, getting on or facing someone? Then に. Leaving, passing through or acting on a thing? Then を.
